sentences.text:
Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal
 Office Notes,
Sl. Date reports,
No. orders or Court'S Or Judge'S Order
S  proceedings  or directions  and  Registrar's  order with  Signatures  C482 No. 918 of 2024  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Abhishek Verma, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Dheeraj Joshi, learned counsel holding brief of Ms. Aishwarya Thapliyal, learned counsel for the complainant.

4. Present C482 application has been moved along with the compounding application (IA No. 1 of 2024) supported with the affidavits of all the applicants and respondent nos. 2 to 4.
5.
Applicant-Mohd. Waseem and respondent Shama Parveen are present in the Court and are duly identified by their respective counsel.
6. The applicant married with respondent no. 2/complainant on 30.03.2020 and from this wed-lock there is no issue and they are living separately since October 2020.

This Court also interacted with both the parties particularly with the complainant and she submits that both have now decided to live separately and will get divorce as per law and towards permanent alimony, the applicant who is a carpenter has paid a sum of Rs. 2 lakhs and on interaction respondent no. 2 submits that she is happy with this amount and she does not want more from the present applicant and she has a great desire to get separation from this relation.
7.
It is also submitted by both the parties that they will move a divorce petition as early as possible before the appropriate Court as per law relating to their religion.

8. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State submits that the offences punishable under Sections 377, 498 IPC read with Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act are non compoundable but he fairly submits that the allegation appears to be of matrimonial dispute which the parties have C482/918/2024 on 6 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7981584/
1 settled and now both of them decided to live separately and also towards permanent alimony Rs.2 lakhs has already been paid by the applicant to respondent no. 2, therefore, there is no useful purpose to continue this proceeding particularly when respondent/ complainant herself submits that she settled the dispute with the applicant
, therefore, the offences can be compounded.

9. Keeping in view the fact that the allegations appears to be matrimonial in nature and the parties have settled their dispute amicable, this Court is of the view that compounding application deserves to be allowed.

Proceeding of Criminal Case No. 21 of 2022,
arising out of FIR No. 371 of 2020, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 377, 504 and 506 IPC and under Section 3/4 of D.P. Act pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate, Jaspur District Udham Singh Nagar is hereby quashed.
